newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, settles in range.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, settles in range.

text.p: Precious metals prices seemed to be settling into range trading on Thursday in markets which lacked fresh input and direction, dealers said.
Most of the interest was focused on the platinum group metals (PGMs) although dealers said volumes were fairly light so far there too.
A slightly easier dollar against the mark, Swiss franc and yen might have been a mild background support, they said.
Gold was fixed at $326.00 per ounce down from $327.55 previously and a London close of $326.40/$326.90.
The New York Comex gold futures market closed only marginally higher yesterday and gold came off fractionally with the dollar in Tokyo and settle a further 30 cents or so lower in a quiet Hong Kong.
Far East dealers said Chinese demand was likely to drop off during August while people celebrated the Hungry Ghosts festival but Indian demand was picking up ahead of the festival season.
"There is physical interest at the bottom of the range but there is selling into rises," a dealer said.
He said some of the selling was from producers but it was not aggressive.
Gold has failed several times recently to break through $328.00-$330.00 resistance with a technical target of $336.00.
Silver was very quiet but it was marked up with gold to $4.39/$4.41, up two cents and was seen consolidating.
"It is not overbought but it looks toppy at $4.40," one dealer said, noting that a new lease of life would only arrive if silver got well past $4.40 where it has failed before.
A report that the Lithuanian central bank was considering selling its gold reserves was not a market factor, dealers said.
The bank's reserves are valued at $62.1 million would total nearly six tonnes of metal at today's price.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer but quiet.
Platinum fixed at $429.00 down a dollar and palladium was up $2.00 at $211.00, its highest fixing since June 11.
Dealers said further short covering by investors on Tocom facing margin calls had supported prices overnight.
Dealers said they were unsure of any market impact from U.S. producer Stillwater Mining Co electing to deliver against its 1997 forward sales rather than roll them forward.
High prices this year and the market backwardation were behind the company's decision
"This would certainly free up metal, but it is difficult to estimate the impact without more information," a dealer said.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
